## Claims
- [source-backed] Inspected formal source: `sources/0809.2981v2.tex`, revision `source-revision-9f2d90286b159738da58b0fe0bd47f85b5597dcdbd2b987cea65817b43536281`. It states: “The \(\ZZ\)-basis for \(\Lambda\) given by the Schur functions \(s_\lambda\)” and that \(I_{r,n-r}\), “spanned by all \(s_\lambda\) with \(\lambda\not\subseteq(n-r)^r\), forms an ideal”; it further identifies the in-box classes \(\{s_\lambda:\lambda\subseteq(n-r)^r\}\) as a \(\ZZ\)-basis. [source-2, lines 1312-1330]
- [proved] Therefore \(\Lambda/I_{r,n-r}\) is a free abelian group with basis \(\{\bar s_\lambda:\lambda\subseteq(n-r)^r\}\): quotient the direct Schur decomposition of \(\Lambda\) by the direct summand spanned by the out-of-box Schur functions. The source’s ideal statement makes this a quotient-ring basis. [source-2, lines 1318-1324]
- [unsupported] The supplied formal excerpts contain no Littlewood–Richardson or Pieri multiplication formula in the quotient, such as \(\bar s_\lambda\bar s_\mu=\sum_{\nu\subseteq(n-r)^r}c_{\lambda\mu}^{\nu}\bar s_\nu\) or the horizontal-strip specialization for \(h_k\bar s_\lambda\). The cited generating-family passage only states ideal generation. [source-2, lines 1312-1330; source-2, lines 1363-1375; source-2, lines 1384-1400]
- [proved] The requested combined source certificate is **not established** from the supplied source record: its integral in-box Schur-basis portion is established, but its quotient LR/Pieri-multiplication portion lacks a stable formal-source excerpt.

## Strategy
Use the quotient’s explicitly stated integral Schur decomposition; do not infer an unstated LR/Pieri rule from the generating-family result.

## Gaps
A formal-source excerpt explicitly stating, or proving, the integral LR rule and Pieri rule after quotienting by \(I_{r,n-r}\) is missing.

## Next
Provide a formal-source passage with the quotient LR/Pieri formula, with stable line locators.
